exact_statement: If P_n converges weakly to P on C([0,1],C) with the uniform metric, define E(r,q) by existence of s<t with endpoint distance <=r and intervening subcurve diameter >=q. Then P has no nonconstant self-return almost surely if and only if for every q>0, lim_{r down to 0} limsup_{n to infinity} P_n(E(r,q))=0.
assumptions: Weak convergence in the uniform metric on continuous parametrized curves
proof_or_counterexample: E(r,q) is closed by compactness of the witnessing times and continuity of subcurve diameter; intersect as r decreases. Use the closed-set weak-convergence inequality for necessity and the strict open event U(r,q) plus the open-set inequality for sufficiency. A countable union over q=1/k excludes all positive-diameter returns.
